title: The Tony Parente record date
summary: Wiggs recalls the two sides, In the Dungeon and When You and I Were Pals, with Stratigas, Buzzy Williams and Monk Hazel, and the engineer complaining about his volume.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Let's see, while we're talking about recording dates, can you tell us anything about Tony Parente's dates? They were the Colombias, weren't they? Are Victor's? Wait a minute, let me think. I believe it was
either OK or Colombia. I can't remember.
Some were on Victor and some are Colombias, mostly.
Well, I mean, the date I was on, I don't know anything at all about the others.
Were you only on one date? Yeah, I was only on
Yeah. One was called In the Dungeon and the other was when you and I were pals. And on that date there was Tony and Alice Stratigas, I believe, on trombone.
That reminds me, you're on a record he made on Vocalion, is that right? Stratigas?
So I never could find it, never did find it.

I have one. I have a beat up one. Myself, I've been looking for a good copy for years. I've never been able to find it. But on this Tony Parente date, let me see, there was Tony and Alice Stratigas, I think, on trombone. And Buzzy, Buzzy Williams on piano. And Monk Hazel on drums. And myself, just five pieces, I believe.
You only made the two sides. Is that really all you made that day?
Strange in those days you say.

Yeah, and they took a long time and the doggone engineer kept on fussing at me for playing loud. And I wasn't playing loud. I was playing as the lead trumpet should do, should carry the lead in a heavy fashion. But he fussed and fussed at me. I didn't pay much attention to him. I tried to keep as near the volume that I thought was right for the balance as possible and the records turned out all right, I thought.
